Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৩৭) Find the odd one out-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Assiduous= showing great care and perseverance, Unoccupied= not being occupied or used, Quiescent= in a state or period of inactivity or dormancy, Dormant= temporarily inactive.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৩৮) ''Exuberance'' means-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Exuberance= the quality of being full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness, Indifference= lack of interest, concern, or sympathy, Apathy= lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern, Buoyancy= a cheerful and optimistic attitude or disposition, Lethargy= a lack of energy and enthusiasm.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৩৯) Closest opposite in meaning of the word ''Acrimonious''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Acrimonious= (typically of speech or discussion) angry and bitter, Trenchant= vigorous or incisive in expression or style, Pleasant= giving a sense of happy satisfaction or enjoyment, Rancorous= characterized by bitterness or resentment, Tepid = showing little enthusiasm.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪০) Antonym of ''Shrewd''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (CD) Shrewd= having or showing sharp powers of judgement, Astute=having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people, Ingenious=clever, original, and inventive, Frivolous=  carefree and superficial, Wily= skilled at gaining an advantage, especially deceitfully.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪১) Which one is not the meaning of the word ''Sojourn''?
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (Oxford Dictionary): Sojourn= a temporary stay; Lodge= a small house at the gates of a park or on the grounds of a large house, occupied by a gatekeeper, gardener, or other employee; Settle= resolve or reach an agreement about (an argument or problem); Migrate= move from one region or habitat to another according to the seasons; Stopover = a break in a journey.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪২) Which one is the closest in meaning of the word ''Solitude''?
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Solitude= the state or situation of being alone; Seclusion= the state of being private and away from other people; Disorder= a state of confusion; Solvent= able to dissolve other substances.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৩) Which one is the opposite in meaning of the word ''Tedium''?
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Tedium = the state or quality of being tedious; Boredom = the state of feeling bored; Routine = organize according to a routine; Diversion= an activity that diverts the mind from tedious or serious concerns; a recreation or pastime; Doldrums= a state or period of stagnation or depression.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৪) Which one is the opposite in meaning of the word ''Temerity''?
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Temerity= excessive confidence or boldness, audacity; Modesty= the quality of being relatively moderate, limited, or small in amount, rate, or level; Hesitation= the action of pausing before saying or doing something.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৫) Meaning of ''Equivocal''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Equivocal= open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous. Unquestionable= not able to be disputed or doubted. Obvious = easily perceived or understood; clear, self-evident, or apparent. Ambiguous= open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৬) Closest meaning of the word ''Virulent''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Virulent = extremely severe or harmful in its effects, very virulent or infectious. Placid = not easily upset or excited. Wholesome = conducive to or characterized by moral well-being. Malignant = evil in nature or effect; malevolent. Compassionate = feeling or showing sympathy and concern for others.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৭) Closest meaning of the word ''Abeyance''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Abeyance = a state of temporary disuse or suspension. Revival = an improvement in the condition, strength, or fortunes of someone or something. Abominable = very bad; terrible. Abscission = the natural detachment of parts of a plant, typically dead leaves and ripe fruit.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৮) Opposite in meaning of the word ''Debilitate''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Debilitate = make (someone) very weak and infirm. Animate = bring to life. Enfeeble = make weak or feeble. Attenuate = reduce in thickness; make thin. Prostrate = a gland surrounding the neck of the bladder in male mammals and releasing a fluid component of semen.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৪৯) Synonym of ''Eccentric''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Eccentric= (of a person or their behaviour) unconventional and slightly strange. Reasonable= having sound judgement; fair and sensible. Decorous= in keeping with good taste and propriety; polite and restrained. Idiosyncratic= relating to idiosyncrasy; peculiar or individual. Predominant= having or exerting control or power.

Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.question: ৫০) Antonym of the word ''Factitious''-
Quotations and Characters (All Ages) and.exp: (OD) Factitious = artificially created or developed. Simulated = manufactured in imitation of some other material. Whimsical= acting or behaving in a capricious manner. Authentic= of undisputed origin and not a copy; genuine.
